headline: US will NOT attack Iran 'at any time' before the midterms -- directly undercuts Barrack's 'weekend strike absolutely possible
dek: Kelly: the US will not be attacking Iran 'at any time' prior to the midterm elections. She added the blockade 'will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait'.
sources: Anna Kelly, White House spokeswoman, in emailed response to MarketWatch (Friday Oct 23)
fault_line: Is the weekend-strike threat real, or midterm theatre -- does Washington strike before Nov 3, or is the war on pause until the votes are counted?

sections.what_happened: Kelly: the US will not be attacking Iran 'at any time' prior to the midterm elections. She added the blockade 'will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait'. This directly contradicts the weekend-strike possibility raised by US ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack ('Absolutely', Oct 23 interview, recorded in 1100-01) and Trump's 'another little Epic Fury' rally line. MarketWatch also reports WSJ-sourced expectation that Tehran would respond to renewed Israeli/US bombing with strikes on Gulf pipelines and airports, and BCA's Matt Gertken: Trump will intensify strikes after the election to coerce a ceasefire.
sections.what_verified: Single publisher family: the White House statement itself, carried by MarketWatch. PASS GATE NOTE: family_count is 1 because the family IS the primary source (the White House's own position, quoted from its emailed response) -- primary_source_single_family: true, and the claim keeps its PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM label. No second family independently confirmed the email.
sections.what_disputed: Barrack (Oct 23): weekend strike 'absolutely' possible. Trump (Florida rally, Oct 23): 'We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree.' The Kelly line may be midterm messaging rather than a policy commitment -- it does not rule out post-midterm action, and Gertken (BCA, via MarketWatch) explicitly predicts intensified post-election strikes. AAA national average gasoline $4.29/gal (MarketWatch) vs under $3 before the war -- the pocketbook pressure behind the messaging.
sections.why_matters: Washington contradicts itself in 24 hours: one envoy says a strike this weekend is 'absolutely' possible; the White House says no attack before the midterms. Both cannot be the plan.
